# **Fighter**

***Fighters share an unparalleled mastery with weapons and armor, and a thorough knowledge of the skills of combat. They are well acquainted with death, both meting it out and staring it defiantly in the face.***  
*You must have a Dexterity or Strength modifier of \+1 or higher in order to multiclass in or out of this class.*

## **Class Features**

### **Vitals**

**Hit Dice:** 1d10  
**Hit Points at 1st Level**: 10 \+ your Constitution modifier  
**Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d10 (or 6\) \+ your Constitution modifier per fighter level after 1st  
**Stress Points at 1st Level:** 3 \+ your Constitution modifier

### **Proficiencies**

**Armor:** All armor, shields  
**Weapons:** Simple weapons, martial weapons  
**Tools:** None  
**Skills:** Choose two skills from Acrobatics, Animal Handling, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Perception, and Survival

### **Equipment**

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

* (a) light, medium, or heavy armor  
* (a) a martial weapon and a light, medium, or heavy shield (b) two martial weapons  
* (a) two simple weapons  
* (a) a dungeoneer's pack or (b) an explorer's pack

### **Fighting Style**

You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

* **Archery (PHB).** You gain a \+2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.  
* **Blind Fighting (TCE).** You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.  
* **Defense (PHB).** While you are wearing armor, you gain a \+1 bonus to your Absorb, even if the armor does not normally have Absorb.  
* **Dual Wielding (PHB).** You can use two-weapon fighting as long as one of the weapons you are holding has the Light property.  
* **Dueling (PHB).** When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a \+2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.  
* **Great Weapon Fighting (PHB).** When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can change the roll to be a 3\. This can only apply to a single damage die per attack.  
* **Interception (TCE).** When a creature within 5 ft. of you that you can see is attacked, you can use your reaction to shift the target of the attack to be yourself.  
* **Protection (PHB).** When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll.  
* **Thrown Weapon Fighting (TCE).** You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.  
  * In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a \+2 bonus to the damage roll.  
* **Unarmed Fighting (TCE).** Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 \+ your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren't wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8. When you succeed a Shove or Grapple attack against a creature, they take damage equal to your Strength modifier.

### **Martial Prowess**

Your training as a soldier or warrior has imparted on you various techniques to utilize against your foes. You know two Prowesses from the Fighter prowess list.

**Prowesses Known.** The Fighter table shows how many Prowesses you know at 1st level and higher. When you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Martial Prowesses you know and replace it with another Prowess from the Fighter prowess list.

**Prowess Ability.** Strength or Dexterity, whichever is higher, is your Prowess ability for your fighter prowesses, as the power of your abilities relies on your physical capacity. You use your Strength or Dexterity whenever a prowess refers to your prowess ability. In addition, you use your Strength or Dexterity modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a fighter Prowess you use.

**Prowess save DC** \= 8 \+ your proficiency bonus \+ your Strength or Dexterity modifier

### **Warrior’s Grit**

Starting at 2nd level, you can make your abilities more potent. When a creature makes a saving throw against your Prowess save DC and succeeds, you can take a Stress to force them to reroll the die.

### **Martial Archetype**

At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate in your combat styles and techniques. The archetype you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

| Martial Archetype |  |  |  |  |
| :---- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Champion |  |  |  |  |

### **Trait Improvement**

When you reach 2nd level, and again at 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can improve upon one of your traits listed below. You have the following choices:

* Gain an additional Stress Slot  
* Gain a \+1 bonus to a Saving Throw  
* Gain a \+1 bonus to your Initiative  
* Gain proficiency in a skill, tool, or language. This option may only be chosen twice.

### **Ability Improvement**

When you reach 4th level, and again at 6th, 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase two ability modifiers of your choice by 1\. Alternatively, you can increase only one ability modifier of your choice by 1 and gain a Feat. As normal, you can't increase an ability modifier above \+5 using this feature.

### **Extra Attack**

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level in this class and to four when you reach 20th level in this class.

### **Signature Prowess**

Beginning at 5th level, you can choose a Martial Prowess to make your signature. When you use that Prowess for the first time, rotate the card instead of flipping it. When you use a rotated Prowess, you then flip it. When you gain a level in this class, you can

The number of Signature Prowesses you have increases to two at 9th level and to three at 13th level.

### **Martial Master**

When you reach 20th level, you have reached the pinnacle of a warrior. When you apply your Signature Prowess to an attack, you can choose to take the maximum damage instead of rolling dice. Additional attacks you make as a part of that action does not use this value.

# **Battle Master**

***Those who emulate the archetypal Battle Master employ martial techniques passed down through generations. To a Battle Master, combat is an academic field, sometimes including subjects beyond battle such as weaponsmithing and calligraphy. Not every fighter absorbs the lessons of history, theory, and artistry that are reflected in the Battle Master archetype, but those who do are well-rounded fighters of great skill and knowledge.***

| Battle Master |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Level** | **Features** |
| 3rd | Combat Superiority, Student of War |
| 7th | Know Your Enemy |
| 10th | Improved Combat Superiority |
| 15th | Relentless |
| 18th | Art of War |

## **Combat Superiority**

When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you have honed your Prowesses to strike harder than ever. When you use a Martial Prowess as part of an attack, such as the Pushing Strike Prowess, you may take a Stress to add 1d10 to the damage roll.

## **Know Your Enemy**

Starting at 7th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if the creature is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice:

* Strength modifier  
* Dexterity modifier  
* Constitution modifier  
* Armor Class  
* Total Absorb  
* Current stress slots  
* Current hit points  
* Total class levels, if any  
* Fighter class levels, if any

## **Improved Combat Superiority**

At 10th level, you may add a d8 to the damage roll when you use a Martial Prowess as part of an attack without taking Stress.

## **Relentless**

Starting at 15th level, when you start your turn with no Prowesses remaining, you may unflip a Prowess of your choice. Additionally, you can flip a Prowess of your choice at the end of your turn, but you do not gain any of its effects.

## **Art of War**

Starting at 18th level, you have achieved a mastery of combat. As a Minor Action, you may expend a Heroic Inspiration to unflip all of your Martial Prowesses.
